cards.prose: The spirit knows exactly who Yahusha (Jesus) is and says it out loud, and James says the same of the devils, that they *believe, and tremble*. Naming him rightly costs the spirit nothing, and it is not the same as belonging to him or doing what he says.
cards.member_sentence: James says even the devils believe in one Elohim (God) and tremble, which is what the unclean spirit does when it meets Yahusha (Jesus).

cards.prose: The spirit calls him Son of the Most High, and the title goes back to Abram's day. Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) met him as *the priest of the El Elyon (most high God)*, so the one the legion begs by is the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the man in the tombs is standing in front of his Son.
cards.member_sentence: Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) brings bread and wine to Abram as priest of the El Elyon (most high God), the same title the spirit uses.

cards.prose: Matthew has the ruler say his daughter *is even now dead*. Mark has her still living, *at the point of death*, and the father pleading greatly for Yahusha (Jesus) to come while there is time. Mark lets us stand in the hour before the news comes from the house.
cards.member_phrase: My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay thy hand upon her, and she shall live
cards.member_sentence: Matthew gives the ruler's plea after the child has already died, asking Yahusha (Jesus) to lay his hand on her so that she shall live.

cards.prose: Mark gives the father's words about the girl, and Luke tells us where he wanted Yahusha (Jesus) to go, *into his house*. He was *a ruler of the synagogue*, a man of standing, and he fell down at the feet of the one the rulers would soon turn against.
cards.member_phrase: there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue
cards.member_sentence: Luke names Jairus, says he was a ruler of the synagogue, and has him fall at Yahusha's (Jesus's) feet asking him into his house.

cards.prose: Moses wrote the rule down, and nothing in Mark says it was wrong. For as long as the issue ran she was unclean, and for her that meant twelve years. What Mark shows is that when she touched Yahusha (Jesus) the cleanness went out of him into her, and the uncleanness did not pass to him.
cards.member_phrase: if a woman have an issue of her blood many days out of the time of her separation
cards.member_sentence: Leviticus says the woman whose flow runs on past its time is unclean all the days of the issue, which is the twelve years Mark counts.

cards.prose: Mark does not say yet what she touched, but Numbers says what a garment of a man of Yashar'el (Israel) carried, *fringes in the borders of their garments* with a blue cord, there to make him remember the commandments. She comes up behind a man wearing what Moses commanded.
cards.member_sentence: Numbers commands fringes with a blue cord on the borders of the garments so that Yashar'el (Israel) would remember all the commandments and do them.

cards.prose: Jeremiah promises a righteous Branch for David, and in his days *Yahudah (Judah) shall be saved, and Yashar'el (Israel) shall dwell safely*. A woman shut out for twelve years by the uncleanness Leviticus names is made whole by touching the one who carries the name Jeremiah gives that Branch, *Yahuah Tsidkenu (THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS)*.
cards.member_sentence: Jeremiah says both houses are saved and dwell safely in the days of the righteous Branch, who is named as our righteousness.
cards.flag: The old note says the Torah's uncleanness is 'fulfilled'; I kept to Jeremiah's own words and did not say the uncleanness rules were set aside.

cards.prose: He calls her *Daughter* in front of the crowd, and tells her it was her trust. Habakkuk says the just shall live by his faith, and what the woman did is that faith walked out. She heard of him, came up behind, and reached for the border of his garment.
cards.member_sentence: Habakkuk sets the proud soul beside the just man who lives by his faith, the trust the woman showed in reaching for him.

cards.prose: The woman had tried everything for twelve years and was still failing, and the psalmist knows that place. He says *I had fainted* unless he believed he would see the goodness of Yahuah (the LORD) in *the land of the living*. She believed she would see it in her own body while she lived.
cards.member_sentence: The psalmist would have fainted had he not believed he would see the goodness of Yahuah (the LORD) in the land of the living.

cards.prose: The verse that says *surely ye shall not be established* unless you believe is the one that names Ephraim, the house about to be scattered. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the woman her believing made her whole, and in a few verses he asks the same of a ruler.
cards.member_phrase: If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says that without believing there is no standing, and the verse that says it names Ephraim, whose head is Samaria.

cards.prose: Word has just come that the girl is dead, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers the father with the trust that kept the psalmist from fainting, believing *to see the goodness* of Yahuah (the LORD) in *the land of the living*. Jairus is asked to go on believing while the report says there is nothing left to see.
cards.member_sentence: The psalmist held on to seeing the goodness of Yahuah (the LORD) while he lived, which is what Jairus is told to hold on to.
